T1: Individual consumers will adopt a differentiated hearing-protection product if it offers a compelling, non-functional benefit such as fashion, status, or integration with lifestyle activities, because they view protection as a lifestyle accessory rather than a medical necessity. Who benefits: Consumers seeking to express personal style or align with trendy activities.. Why behaviour changes: When a product is marketed as a fashion item or integrated into activities like music, outdoor recreation, or work, consumers are motivated to purchase it for status and convenience rather than purely for safety.. How value is captured: Hellberg can charge premium prices, sell multiple units per consumer (e.g., different colors or models), and leverage direct-to-consumer channels to capture higher margins.. Assumptions: Consumers associate hearing protection with personal expression rather than solely functional need.; Marketing can effectively frame the product as a lifestyle accessory.; There is sufficient willingness to pay a premium for non-functional benefits.. Predictions: In a test offering a fashion-oriented version of the product at a higher price point, purchase intent or actual sales will exceed that of a standard safety version.; Surveyed consumers will cite style, status, or activity integration as primary reasons for purchase..

T2: Individual consumers will adopt a differentiated hearing-protection product if it is positioned as a safety-critical, high-performance solution for a specific activity (e.g., music, industrial work, outdoor recreation), because they rely on proven protection and are willing to pay for reliability. Who benefits: Consumers who engage in activities where hearing loss is a risk and need reliable protection.. Why behaviour changes: When a product is marketed as the industry‑standard or the only choice for a particular use case, consumers trust the brand and are willing to purchase it even at higher prices, because they perceive it as essential for safety.. How value is captured: Hellberg can command premium pricing, sell through specialized channels (e.g., music stores, industrial distributors), and build brand reputation as the go‑to‑solution for that segment.. Assumptions: Consumers prioritize safety over price for critical protection.; A differentiated proposition emphasizing industry certification or activity‑specific performance will be perceived as a competitive advantage.; There is a measurable segment of consumers actively seeking high‑performance hearing protection for a specific activity.. Predictions: In a test offering a safety‑focused version of the product at a premium price, purchase intent or actual sales will exceed that of a generic safety version.; Surveyed consumers will cite safety reliability, industry endorsement, or activity‑specific performance as primary reasons for purchase..

Test "DIY vs Small Operator Marine Coating Test" between T1; T2. Method: Online survey with simulated purchase scenario. Recruit 200 respondents: 100 DIY boat owners (recruited via marine forums and DIY groups) and 100 small marine operators (recruited via charter boat associations and fishing groups). Each participant views a product description for a Jotun marine coating emphasizing either (a) clear instructions and biofouling protection (DIY version) or (b) reduced downtime and cost savings (small operator version). They are then asked to state their maximum willingness to pay (WTP) in euros and their likelihood to purchase (1‑10 scale).. Sample: 200 participants (100 DIY, 100 small operators). Measure: Average WTP (euros) and purchase intent score for each version.. Predictions: T1: DIY version yields higher average WTP and higher purchase intent than small operator version.; T2: Small operator version yields higher average WTP and higher purchase intent than DIY version.. Decision rule: If DIY version’s average WTP ≥ €150 and purchase intent ≥ 6/10, proceed with differentiated consumer proposition targeting DIY. If small operator version’s average WTP ≥ €150 and purchase intent ≥ 6/10, proceed with differentiated consumer proposition targeting small operators. If neither version meets thresholds, recommend no expansion.. Cost: 15000 euros, 10 weeks.

Favours T1: Do not invest in a differentiated consumer proposition at this time. Conduct the proposed DIY vs Small Operator Marine Coating Test (X1) to empirically compare willingness to pay and purchase intent for the two value propositions before any expansion decision. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two product descriptions: (A) DIY boat owner kit emphasizing biofouling protection and clear instructions; (B) Small marine operator kit emphasizing durability and reduced downtime. Both descriptions include Jotun product name, price (15% above standard marine coating), and a brief description of the coating’s marine-grade performance. Participants indicate whether they would purchase the kit and the maximum price they would pay. The test will run for 12 weeks, with 500 participants per group (total 1,000).. Sample: 1,000 DIY boat owners and small marine operators recruited via marine forums, social media, and professional networks in Scandinavia and the UK.. Measure: Purchase intent (binary: would buy) and willingness to pay (EUR).. Predictions: T1: Group A will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Group B.; T2: Group B will show higher purchase intent and willingness to pay than Group A.. Decision rule: If the difference in purchase intent between Group A and Group B exceeds 10 percentage points (e.g., Group A at 45% and Group B at 35%), proceed to develop a differentiated consumer proposition targeting the higher‑intent segment. If the difference is less than 5 percentage points, conclude insufficient evidence to justify a differentiated proposition. If the difference is between 5‑10 percentage points, conduct a second test with a larger sample to confirm.. Cost: 20000 euros, 12 weeks.

Based on medical evidence linking excess body fat to heart disease, diabetes and certain cancers, Tanita introduced the world’s first integrated body composition analyzer/scale to the professional markets in 1992.
Tanita is a world leader in precision electronic scales. With almost 50% of its domestic market share, the name Tanita is a household name in Japan.
